origin_result.basis: A 6-digit HS code is required for non-originating input BOM row 2 (Emollients).

procedure.step: The Ministry of Economy and Tourism requires factory registration through its Factory Registration service prior to certificate application, taking about 3 working days.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: The Ministry of Foreign Trade provides the Certificate of Origin for India e-service for local manufacturers and exporters.
The competent authority issues the certificate of origin prior to, at, or within five (5) working days of the date of exportation.
Pay the certificate of origin fee of AED 50 charged by the Ministry of Foreign Trade for invoice values up to AED 100,000.

The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry and must hold origin information under CAROTAR 2020; electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to e-Sanchit (unconfirmed).
The exporter must keep origin records, including cost breakdowns, for at least 5 years starting from the end of the calendar year of issue.

caveats.note: Estimate on the shipment value given. India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ. Shown in the shipment's own currency; never converted.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
'+' in a rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
